task1_center_stratified_cv.plain_language_summary: A 1-fold pilot with the exact winning XGBoost config on the 948-feature MAF matrix shows the MAF-vs-burden gap is 0.505 under standard CV and 0.496 under center-stratified CV - a change of only 0.009. This confirms the published 5-fold finding (gap 0.502 -> 0.497): center-stratified folds do not collapse the representation ranking. The full 5-fold rerun was not completed because each 948-feature 20-class XGBoost model takes 15-20 minutes (20 models = 5+ hours). The 1,130-feature Sig+MAF winner could not be tested because the TCGA signature matrix is not on this machine; the 948-feature MAF matrix was used as the closest available substitute.

reconciliation.reviewer_question: Was the ablation run on a different pipeline, seed, or split? (0.760/0.900 vs headlines 0.777/0.911)
reconciliation.answer: No. Same pipeline, same folds, different estimator.

evidence.ablation_pipeline: scripts/run_hrd_shortcut_ablation.py: seed 20260820, 5 outer folds, nested inner-validation tuning - same procedure as benchmark
evidence.ablation_estimator: pooled_global_oof (single metric on concatenated out-of-fold predictions)
evidence.headline_estimator: fold-mean (mean of 5 per-fold scores, with t-based 95% CIs)

reconciliation.conclusion: The 0.760/0.900 vs 0.777/0.911 discrepancy is fully explained by pooled-OOF vs fold-mean estimators, not by different pipelines/seeds/splits. The ablation's substantive finding stands: removing all 32 per-gene features for the 16 HRR genes leaves HRD performance essentially unchanged (Spearman +0.002, p=0.62; AUROC -0.001, p=0.64). A fold-mean rescoring of the ablation requires the HRD labels, which are not on this machine.

The ablation's conclusion (HRR-gene features are dispensable for HRD prediction) is unaffected.
